Params: The lighthouse burns bright as a torch of starlight, but its glow cannot chase away the shadows pressing in from all sides. Alarm sirens spiral overhead, their wail never ceasing.
Everyone to open ground! Stay clear of falling rock!
The awakened island convulses, shaking sand and stone and trees from its back until the vast metal spine beneath lies bare.
From above, colossal mechanical arms plummet without pattern, each collision of steel and rock landing like a hammer blow.
The Mannan M-1A is the largest marine engineering unit ever built, but even then... it shouldn't be anything like this.
The Punishing Virus has gotten into it! There's no fighting something that size.
Captain, this is bad! The protocol broke down! We've lost control of the lighthouse!
The data's starting to flow into the buffer pool again... Captain Karenina... is that good news or bad news?
The grave expression on Karenina's face says everything.
Far off, the sea begins to roil with a sickly red, and the dark crimson tide creeps steadily toward the island.
The lifeboat from the surface operation should still be at the dock. Get to it and get off this island.
The Construct girl surveys her surroundings.
Sava freezes for a moment, then turns to look as well.
Before everything went off, I think I saw her heading toward the lighthouse.
Karenina's brow furrows for a moment.
(The lighthouse is the critical node. If she's there... at least she's out of the path of those mechanical arms.)
We should move. Let's get to the lifeboat at the dock first.
Karenina guards the group as everyone pushes toward the dock.
The lifeboat's engine growls to life with a low hum.
Once the last person climbs aboard, Karenina presses both hands against the gunwale, shoves the boat away, and jumps back onto the dock.
The protocol broke down. If I don't retake control before this thing spirals, we lose everything.
...You know what happens if we do nothing. Arius gets the cables back.
You'd just be in my way. Tripping over your own feet while I'm trying to work.
This is captain business. Let your captain handle it!
Listen to me. What happens next isn't a repeater swap. It's not something rookies can fix on the fly.
Skilled techs are hard to replace. We... need to save every one we can.
So get the idea of going down with the ship out of your heads, and get out!
Karenina looks toward Larsen, carefully avoiding your eyes at the stern.
My team is in your hands now... And get 【kuroname】 out safe.
Karenina fulfills her role as captain, and her command over her people is not yours to challenge. And yet...
You understand there is no time for disputes. The choice has already settled inside you.
Larsen's lips move, barely, and stay silent.
Karenina holds your gaze for one long, heavy moment. Then she shoves the boat away and runs toward the island, never once looking back.
You watch her silhouette shrink into the distance and let out a quiet sigh.
I'm not leaving her behind. I have to go back.
There is no time to argue with Karenina over who stays behind. It is better to act first and explain later.
I have to go back. I won't let her do this alone.
Right now, I'm the only one who can maintain a M.I.N.D. connection with her. If something goes wrong, I can back her up.
Larsen, this boat is yours now. Be a good captain.
Without waiting for Larsen to answer, you rise to your feet and leap across the stretch of water before the boat can drift too far from the dock.
Then you chase in the direction Karenina went.
The island's paths lie in ruins, smashed apart by the mechanical arms. Karenina sprints alone through the shattered stone and loose gravel.
A sharp alarm shrieks from her terminal.
She looks down. The data streams are vanishing from the screen, swallowed piece by piece, and in their place, scattered pixels begin to assemble.
They stitch together into the smiling face of a man.
Do you still believe you have a way out?
Every muscle in the girl's frame locks tight at once.
Good. That expression tells me everything.
The voice that comes through the virtual screen carries a gentleness that chills her to the bone.
You don't know a damn thing about me.
Losing one's sense of self... I imagine it's rather unpleasant.
But no matter. You'll have an eternity to adjust. Assuming, of course... that what remains of "you" still understands the concept of adjustment.
He pauses, giving her a moment to absorb his words.
If you won't walk beside me...
His smile grows a little wider.
...then you'll simply have to resume your role as my finest test subject.
Karenina fixes her gaze on the calm face on the screen, her golden eyes blazing as if about to catch fire.
Ah, that look. I know it well.
Do struggle for me. I'll be watching every moment. Don't disappoint.
His face slowly dissolves from the terminal's display.
What remains on the screen is a long, weighted sigh.
A mere test subject? What a waste... Wouldn't you agree, Karenina?
The terminal fades to black, as though the strange encounter never took place.
The sea wind sweeps against Karenina's back. Under Arius' command, the Red Tide rides the swift currents, its edges drawing nearer by the second.
Anger, resentment, and a strange, unnamed pain seize her where she stands, rooting her feet to the ground and giving the one who follows a chance to finally close the distance.
By the time you hurry close enough to see Karenina's back, the sea wind has already stolen all but the last few words.
Karenina whips around, then hurriedly averts her eyes.
Didn't I tell you to evacuate with the others?!
What test subject? Are you hiding something from me?
I didn't want to slow down the mission. And I... I didn't want you all making a huge deal out of nothing!
Tell me. What is this test subject thing about?
Karenina averts her gaze, as though she is wrestling with how to say it.
...We need to get to the lighthouse first!
It is, without question, the most urgent priority. But the way Karenina strides forward also feels like she is running from something else.
Professionally speaking, we should share all intelligence. No exceptions.
The wind streaks past your sides as you race forward.
Her pace, once a reckless sprint, slows to nearly nothing.
Karenina knows that laying everything bare is her best move now.
She draws a deep breath and tells it all in the fewest words she can manage.
She speaks of the body modifications forced on her when she was barely more than an infant, and of how Mara and Wise covered it all up during her Construct surgery.
She speaks of the pain the whale calls bring, the danger of opening a repeater to touch the crystal interference directly, and how the Ytterbium-174 isotope still disrupts her M.I.N.D. even now.
How is your frame right now? Is any of this reversible?
Rarana keeps it stable. The suppression is holding, for now.
Once we finish with Arius, I'll get a full checkup back on Babylonia...
Grandpa left Rarana behind for a reason. Rarana can "heal" me temporarily. Maybe he already found the solution...
And if Rarana can keep me steady, the Science Council can figure out the rest.
You should have told me sooner.
Why? So you could fuss over me? We both knew the repeaters had to be fixed. That part was never up for debate.
No more secrets, not from me.
Karenina faces away from you and walks on.
In the end, she still holds something back.
She did not speak of the threat Arius laid upon her.
"Become a part of him." The words coil in her heart like a half-formed curse, and she fears that giving them voice would let them cling to whoever listens.
Right now, holding back does more harm than good. You know that.
Do you still not trust me?
It has nothing to do with mistrust.
(It's because... you are the most hopeless fool I've ever known.)
(I know you would stand in my way. I know, too... that you might actually find a way.)
(Even if it means burning yourself out, even if it means hurting yourself to do it.)
(You care so much about everyone else, but... you've never learned to care about yourself the same way.)
(I'm not letting you carry that weight, at least not this time, when you're with me.)
(No more calculating what must be given up, what must be cut away, just to survive the next hour.)
(I can endure it on my own. I can carry it myself.)
I promise, once Arius is dealt with, everything goes back to normal. Okay?
Can I hold you to that promise?
I already promised! Stop asking! What, you don't believe me now?
Move it! The lighthouse comes first.
There it is again, that old habit. Karenina rushes forward, giving no direct answer.
But the way she leaves her back unguarded before you, open and trusting, might be the only answer you need.
On the far side of the island, Rarana stirs from her slumber and wobbles into the air.
It dodges falling stones and twisted branches, following a familiar pull that leads it to an empty clearing where nothing remains.
Rarana does not know why it came here, but something inside it whispers that this place holds what matters most.
She begins to scratch at the dirt, even though its four small mechanical claws can barely make a mark in the earth.
As though it were its own limb, a mechanical arm suspended high above answers its call and plunges deep into the soil.
The earth splits open, and the closer it gets, the sharper the sensation becomes.
A massive explosion echoes in the distance, followed by a human shout. It is Karenina's voice.
Rarana drifts back into the air.
Rarana knows its friends are fighting.
It knows, too, that the massive mechanical claws bearing down on them are no different from the arm it commands so freely.
Its friends are being attacked by something that is, in a way, "itself."
The great mechanical arm keeps digging, tireless, tearing through layers of gravel and stone as it burrows into the darkness below.
It digs toward the truth hidden in Rarana's fractured memories.
At last, the tip strikes something solid. A pale gray alloy pod.
The moment the sight is registered, buried grief awakens.
Before her stretches a deep, ink-dark ocean, and when her eyes lift, the heavens crack open with jagged veins of lightning.
Why lie to me... Why leave me?
Her true body calls to her, the one corrupted by the Punishing Virus and reshaped by the Red Tide.
That is who she used to be.
That is who she used to be.
Why lie to me... Why leave me?
She is a ghost of the old world, abandoned when the new one moved on.
In the very moment she gained new life, she also died.
...I never went to the new world.
I've been looking for you. Waiting for you.

The mechanical arm she commands rises slowly into the air and reaches toward the churning crimson sea, the way a child stands on tiptoe for the first time, straining to see the world outside the window.
The sounds of battle do not stop. The arms slam into the water, and spray erupts in a towering wall of white mist.
The body that no longer belongs to her is now hunting the friends she treasures most.
That is the home she once escaped. In her consciousness, that body has transformed into a sea of crimson despair.
Somewhere in that red ocean beats a wicked heart. It is not her "heart."
To control the entire Jormungandr node, Arius has condensed a fragment of his consciousness through the Red Tide and lodged this projection inside the giant crab's body.
Through the thin thread still linking her to her original form, Rarana catches a shadowed glimpse of the monster's plan.
That monster wants to eat Karenina...
Going back... means being eaten. That monster will eat me too...
That body has not belonged to her for a long time. If she sinks into that crimson sea, she may never escape again.
On the far side of the island, the mechanical arm begins to stir once more.
But that is family out there.
But that is family out there.
She was a clumsy little crab first, then a clumsy potted plant, never built for complex thoughts.
Yet the simplest law of all is protecting those you love.
And she lets herself sink into the crimson sea of despair.
The mechanical arms, twisting savagely in the air, suddenly lock into place.
